title: Intersection Products on Smooth Projective Surfaces

items.title: Degree of an invertible sheaf on a proper one-dimensional scheme
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the Euler-characteristic supplier. Let k be a field and let C be a proper k-scheme whose underlying Noetherian topological space has dimension at most one. For an invertible O_C-module L define deg_C(L) := chi(C,L) - chi(C,O_C) in Z, and for a locally free O_C-module E of finite constant rank n define deg_C(E) := chi(C,E) - n*chi(C,O_C). Both are well-defined integers, deg_C(O_C) = 0, and deg_C depends only on the isomorphism class of the sheaf. If C is empty every degree is zero. The structure sheaf, its dual and every invertible or locally free finite-rank module are coherent, so the Euler characteristic applies; the dimension bound is what makes the defining alternating sum finite.
items.strategy: Assemble the definition from def-euler-characteristic-coherent-sheaf: on a proper k-scheme, coherent modules have finite-dimensional cohomology vanishing in high degrees, so the alternating sums are integers. Coherence of O_C, of invertible modules and of locally free finite-rank modules is read from def-coherent-module-scheme. Well-definedness on isomorphism classes is immediate because chi is an invariant of the isomorphism class; deg_C(O_C) = chi(C,O_C) - chi(C,O_C) = 0 and the empty case is the empty sum 0.

items.title: Euler characteristic of a closed point, and invariance under an invertible twist
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the Euler-characteristic supplier. Let k be a field, X a proper k-scheme, p in X a closed point with residue field kappa(p), and i: Spec kappa(p) -> X the corresponding closed immersion; write kappa(p) also for the structure sheaf of Spec kappa(p). Then kappa(p) is a coherent O_X-module via i_*, and for every invertible O_X-module L: (1) H^q(X, i_*kappa(p)) = 0 for every q >= 1 and chi(X, i_*kappa(p)) = [kappa(p):k], a finite integer; (2) i^*L is isomorphic to O_{Spec kappa(p)} and there is an isomorphism L (x) i_*kappa(p) isomorphic to i_*kappa(p); consequently chi(X, L (x) i_*kappa(p)) = chi(X, i_*kappa(p)) = [kappa(p):k].
items.strategy: For (1): H^q(X, i_*kappa(p)) is H^q(Spec kappa(p), kappa(p)) by lem-closed-immersion-cohomology-pushforward, the space Spec kappa(p) is Noetherian of dimension zero, so all higher cohomology vanishes by thm-noetherian-topological-space-dimension-vanishing and H^0 = kappa(p) has k-dimension [kappa(p):k]; the residue degree is finite because X is of finite type over k (lem-maximal-ideal-residue-field-of-an-affine-algebra-is-finite). For (2): the stalk of i^*L at the unique point is L_p (x)_{O_{X,p}} kappa(p) = kappa(p) because an invertible module is free of rank one at the local ring, so i^*L is isomorphic to the structure sheaf of Spec kappa(p); then L (x) i_*kappa(p) is a skyscraper supported at p with stalk kappa(p), and the natural map to i_*kappa(p) is an isomorphism by the stalkwise criterion. Applying H^q(X, -) and (1) gives the stated invariance of the Euler characteristic; coherence of i_*kappa(p) is the closed-immersion pushforward clause. The Axiom of Choice is inherited from the Euler-characteristic and devissage suppliers; the argument itself makes no selection.

items.title: Projection formula for a closed immersion and an invertible sheaf
items.statement: Let i: Z -> X be a closed immersion of schemes, L an invertible O_X-module and G a quasi-coherent O_Z-module. Then the canonical map L (x)_{O_X} i_*G -> i_*(i^*L (x)_{O_Z} G) is an isomorphism of O_X-modules. If moreover X is locally Noetherian and G is coherent, then both sides are coherent O_X-modules, and for every q >= 0 there is an isomorphism H^q(X, L (x) i_*G) = H^q(Z, i^*L (x) G); in particular chi(X, L (x) i_*G) = chi(Z, i^*L (x) G) whenever X is proper over a field. The Euler-characteristic and coherence clauses inherit the Axiom of Choice through the Euler-characteristic suppliers, while the stalkwise isomorphism itself is choice-free beyond the cited sheaf and tensor constructions.
items.strategy: Check the canonical map on stalks and conclude by the stalkwise isomorphism criterion. At x not in Z both sides have zero stalk. At x in Z the stalk of i_*G is G_x, the stalk of i^*L is L_x (x)_{O_{X,x}} O_{Z,x}, so the two sides have stalk L_x (x)_{O_{X,x}} G_x and (L_x (x)_{O_{X,x}} O_{Z,x}) (x)_{O_{Z,x}} G_x, which agree by associativity of the tensor product and change of rings. The cohomological statement is the closed-immersion pushforward isomorphism applied to i^*L (x) G; coherence when X is locally Noetherian and G coherent is the pushforward clause of the closed-immersion result. The Axiom of Choice enters only through the Euler-characteristic and coherence suppliers used in the final clause; the stalk computation and the change-of-rings identification make no selection.

items.title: Twisting a coherent sheaf by an invertible sheaf on an integral proper curve
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let k be a field and let X be an integral proper k-scheme whose underlying topological space has dimension one. Let L be an invertible O_X-module and F a coherent O_X-module; let xi be the generic point of X and let r := dim_{kappa(xi)} F_xi be the rank of F. Then chi(X, L (x) F) = r*deg_X(L) + chi(X, F), with deg_X as in def-degree-invertible-sheaf-proper-dimension-one.
items.strategy: Devissage on the Noetherian scheme X, which is finite type hence Noetherian over the field. Consider the property P(F): 'chi(X, L (x) F) = r(F)*deg_X(L) + chi(X, F)'. P is additive in short exact sequences: tensoring with an invertible module is exact (stalks are free of rank one, thm-exactness-of-sheaves-stalkwise), chi is additive (lem-euler-characteristic-additive-short-exact) and the rank r is additive because the stalk at the generic point is a short exact sequence of kappa(xi)-vector spaces and dimension is additive; P(0) holds. The integral closed subschemes of the integral one-dimensional X are X and the closed points. For Z = X take G = O_X, for which P holds by the definition of deg_X(L) and r = 1. For a closed point Z = {p} take G = i_*kappa(p), for which r = 0 and P is exactly lem-euler-characteristic-finite-support-twist-invariance. lem-coherent-devissage-one-generic-generator now gives P(F) for every coherent F. Applying P with F invertible of rank one gives deg_X(L (x) F) = deg_X(L) + deg_X(F). The Axiom of Choice is inherited from the Euler-characteristic and devissage suppliers; the argument itself makes no selection.

items.title: Degree is additive on invertible sheaves over a proper curve
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let k be a field and let C be a proper k-scheme whose underlying topological space has dimension at most one. For all invertible O_C-modules L and M: (1) deg_C(L (x) M) = deg_C(L) + deg_C(M); (2) deg_C(L^vee) = -deg_C(L); (3) chi(C, L (x) M) - chi(C, L) - chi(C, M) + chi(C, O_C) = 0. The curve C need not be reduced, irreducible or normal; closed subschemes of proper k-schemes, in particular effective Cartier divisors on proper surfaces, are the intended instances.
items.strategy: Apply lem-coherent-devissage-one-generic-generator to the property Q(F): 'chi(C,F) - chi(C,L (x) F) - chi(C,M (x) F) + chi(C,L (x) M (x) F) = 0'. Q is additive in short exact sequences because tensoring by invertible modules is exact and chi is additive; Q(0) holds. For an integral closed subscheme Z of C take G = i_*O_Z: if Z is a closed point then every twist of G is G by lem-euler-characteristic-finite-support-twist-invariance, so Q(G) = 0; if Z is one-dimensional then Z is an integral proper curve and lem-closed-immersion-projection-formula-invertible identifies Q_C(i_*O_Z) with Q_Z(O_Z, i^*L, i^*M), which is zero by lem-euler-characteristic-twist-integral-proper-curve applied on Z with F = i^*M of rank one. Devissage gives Q(O_C) = 0, i.e. chi(C,L (x) M) = chi(C,L) + chi(C,M) - chi(C,O_C), which by the definition of degree is (1). Part (2) follows from (1) with M = L^vee and L (x) L^vee = O_C, deg_C(O_C) = 0; part (3) is the displayed form of (1). The Axiom of Choice is inherited from the Euler-characteristic and devissage suppliers; the argument itself makes no selection.

items.title: Intersection numbers of Cartier divisors on a smooth projective surface
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the Euler-characteristic supplier. Let k be a field and let X be an integral, regular, projective k-scheme of pure dimension 2 (a smooth projective surface over k is an instance: smoothness of X over k makes every local ring of X regular). For line bundles L and M on X define L . M := chi(X, O_X) - chi(X, L^vee) - chi(X, M^vee) + chi(X, L^vee (x) M^vee) in Z, and for Cartier divisors C and D on X define C . D := O_X(C) . O_X(D). Then: (1) the value depends only on the isomorphism classes of L and M, so the pairing is a map Pic(X) x Pic(X) -> Z; (2) L . M = M . L and L . O_X = O_X . L = 0; (3) if C' is linearly equivalent to C and D' to D then C' . D' = C . D.
items.strategy: This is a definition: the four Euler characteristics are integers by the definition of chi on the proper k-scheme X, and L^vee, M^vee and L^vee (x) M^vee are invertible hence coherent. Symmetry and L . O_X = 0 are immediate from the displayed formula, and dependence only on isomorphism classes follows from functoriality of the dual and tensor product on Pic. For (3), linear equivalence gives O_X(C') isomorphic to O_X(C) and O_X(D') isomorphic to O_X(D) (thm-cartier-divisors-mod-principal-to-picard together with cartier-divisor-addition-tensor), and (1) applies.

items.title: The surface intersection product is symmetric and bilinear
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let k be a field, let X be an integral regular projective surface over k, and let L, M, N be line bundles on X. Then (L (x) M) . N = L . N + M . N and L . (M (x) N) = L . M + L . N; consequently the intersection product is a symmetric Z-bilinear pairing Pic(X) x Pic(X) -> Z and L . O_X = 0. Equivalently, for Cartier divisors: (C + C') . D = C . D + C' . D, C . (D + D') = C . D + C . D', and C . D = D . C.
items.strategy: Write Phi(C,D) for the defining value, symmetric in C and D. Step 1 (shift identity). Let H be an effective Cartier divisor and L any line bundle. The twisting exact sequences 0 -> O_X(-H) -> O_X -> i_*O_H -> 0 and 0 -> L(-H) -> L -> i_*(L|_H) -> 0 give chi(O_X) - chi(O_X(-H)) = chi(O_H) and chi(L) - chi(L(-H)) = chi(L|_H); applying the second to L = O_X(-C), O_X(-D), O_X(-C-D) and subtracting shows Phi(C, D+H) - Phi(C, D) - Phi(C, H) = -(chi(O_H) - chi(O_H(-C)) - chi(O_H(-D)) + chi(O_H(-C-D))). The bracket is zero by cor-degree-additive-proper-curve(3) applied to the proper curve H (an effective Cartier divisor on an integral surface is a proper scheme of dimension at most one by the principal ideal theorem). Hence Phi(C, D+H) = Phi(C, D) + Phi(C, H). Step 2 (effective additivity). If D2 is effective, Step 1 with H = D2 gives Phi(C, D1+D2) = Phi(C, D1) + Phi(C, D2) for every D1. Step 3 (general additivity). Every Cartier divisor is a difference of effective Cartier divisors: for m large the sheaf O_X(D) (x) O_X(1)^{m} is globally generated (lem-eventual-global-generation-coherent-twists, X projective over the Noetherian field k with O_X(1) ample); a nonzero global section is regular because X is integral, so by lem-global-section-effective-divisor its zero scheme E is an effective Cartier divisor with O_X(E) = O_X(D + mH0), where H0 is the effective Cartier divisor cut by a nonzero section of O_X(1). Writing D_i = E_i - F_i with F_i = m_i H0 and H := E1+E2+F1+F2, Step 1 applied to (D1+D2, H), to (D1, D2+H) and to (D2, H) yields Phi(C, D1+D2) + Phi(C, H) = Phi(C, D1+D2+H) = Phi(C, D1) + Phi(C, D2+H) = Phi(C, D1) + Phi(C, D2) + Phi(C, H); cancelling gives additivity in the second variable. Symmetry gives additivity in the first variable and Phi(C, 0) = 0, so Phi is Z-bilinear; translating to line bundles via the definition gives the statement.

items.title: Intersection with a curve is the degree of the restriction
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let k be a field, X an integral regular projective surface over k, and let C and D be effective Cartier divisors on X, with associated line bundles O_X(C) and O_X(D). Then C . D = deg_C(O_X(D)|_C) = deg_D(O_X(C)|_D), where deg is the degree of def-degree-invertible-sheaf-proper-dimension-one on the proper curves C and D. More generally, if only C is effective, the first identity C . D = deg_C(O_X(D)|_C) holds for every Cartier divisor D on X, with deg_C taken on the curve C. If C is moreover a smooth proper geometrically integral curve, deg_C agrees with the closed-point divisor degree of def-degree-divisor-proper-curve on C. The empty curve case C = emptyset is included: both sides are then 0.
items.strategy: The curve C is a proper k-scheme of dimension at most one (principal ideal theorem), so the degree is available. From 0 -> O_X(-C) -> O_X -> i_*O_C -> 0 one gets chi(O_X) - chi(O_X(-C)) = chi(O_C), and tensoring it with L^vee gives chi(L^vee) - chi(L^vee(-C)) = chi(L^vee|_C). Substituting into the definition of C . D = Phi(C, D) yields C . D = chi(O_C) - chi(L^vee|_C). By the definition of degree on C and cor-degree-additive-proper-curve(2) this is -deg_C(L^vee|_C) = deg_C(L|_C). Exchanging C and D (or using symmetry of the defining formula) gives D . C = deg_D(O_X(C)|_D), and the two right-hand sides therefore agree. The final clause is thm-euler-characteristic-degree-shift-curve, which identifies the chi-degree with the closed-point divisor degree on smooth proper geometrically integral curves.

items.title: The intersection matrix of a point blowup of a regular surface
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field, let
$X$ be an integral regular projective surface over $k$
([[def-divisor-intersection-number-on-smooth-projective-surface]]), let
$p\in X$ be a closed point with residue field $\kappa(p)$ and
$r:=[\kappa(p):k]$, let $\pi:X'=\operatorname{Bl}_pX\to X$ be the blowup of $X$
at $p$ ([[def-blowup-scheme-along-ideal]]) and let
$E:=\pi^{-1}(p)$ be the exceptional curve
([[def-exceptional-divisor-blowup]]). Then:

1. $X'$ is an integral regular projective surface over $k$, $E$ is an effective
   Cartier divisor, $E$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb P^1_{\kappa(p)}$, and
   $\mathcal O_E(E)\cong\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1_{\kappa(p)}}(-1)$; consequently
   $E\cdot E=-r$.
2. For all Cartier divisors $D,D'$ on $X$
   ([[def-cartier-divisor]]): $E\cdot\pi^*D=0$ and
   $\pi^*D\cdot\pi^*D'=D\cdot D'$; in particular $(\pi^*D)^2=D^2$.
3. If $C$ is a reduced effective Cartier divisor on $X$ through $p$ with
   multiplicity $m:=\operatorname{mult}_p(C)\ge1$
   ([[def-effective-cartier-divisor]]) and strict transform $C'$
   ([[def-strict-transform-closed-subscheme]]), then $\pi^*C=C'+mE$,
   $C'\cdot E=mr$ and $C'\cdot C'=C\cdot C-m^2r$. If $p\notin C$ then
   $\pi^*C=C'$ and $(C')^2=C^2$.
items.strategy:
1.1 The ideal $I$ of $p$ is a nonzero coherent ideal on the integral regular projective surface $X$. Thus the blowup is integral, regular and pure of dimension two; $E$ is effective Cartier, isomorphic to $\mathbb P^1_{\kappa(p)}$, with normal line bundle $\mathcal O(-1)$. The residue degree $r$ is finite. To apply the intersection theory, we also verify absolute projectivity. Choose $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^n_k$ and its ample hyperplane bundle $H$. For some $s$, $I\otimes L$, $L=H^{\otimes s}$, is globally generated. A finite set of its global sections generates it: choose finitely many sections spanning each of finitely many affine neighborhoods, possible since $X$ is quasi-compact and the sheaf is of finite type. [F1, F2, F3]

2.1 Put $S=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}I^d\otimes L^{\otimes d}$. The preceding sections yield a graded surjection $\mathcal O_X[z_0,\ldots,z_N]\to S$, since $S$ is generated in degree one. Its relative Proj is canonically $X'$ by invertible rescaling; the twist need not be an ordinary ideal. Hence $X'$ is a closed subscheme of $\mathbb P^N_X$. Base change of $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^n_k$ embeds the latter as a closed subscheme of $\mathbb P^N_k\times_k\mathbb P^n_k$. [F3, step 1.1]

3.1 The product has a closed Segre embedding into $\mathbb P^{(N+1)(n+1)-1}_k$: its coordinates are $z_{ab}=u_av_b$, and the defining equations are all rank-one minors $z_{ab}z_{ij}-z_{aj}z_{ib}$. On $D_+(z_{ij})$, these equations identify its coordinate ring with the polynomial ring on $z_{aj}/z_{ij}$ ($a\ne i$) and $z_{ib}/z_{ij}$ ($b\ne j$); all other coordinates are their products. This is exactly the product of the affine charts $D_+(u_i)$ and $D_+(v_j)$, and the identifications respect their ratio transitions. They glue to the closed embedding. Thus $X'$ is projective over $k$, and all intersection and proper-cohomology hypotheses are satisfied. [F3, F7, step 2.1]

4.1 By the exceptional-curve Euler formula, $\chi_k(E,\mathcal O_E)=r$ and $\chi_k(E,\mathcal O_E(E))=0$, so its degree over $k$ is $-r$. Restriction of the intersection product to the effective curve $E$ gives $E^2=-r$. For any Cartier divisor $D$ on $X$, $\pi|_E$ factors through $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(p)$, since the pulled-back point ideal vanishes on $E$. The restriction of $\pi^*\mathcal O_X(D)$ is therefore trivial. Its degree is zero, and the restriction formula gives $E\cdot\pi^*D=0$. This formula allows arbitrary $D$; only $E$ must be effective. [F1, F4, F6, F7, step 3.1]

4.2 Pushforward vanishing and the projection formula give $\chi(X',\pi^*\mathcal N)=\chi(X,\mathcal N)$ for every invertible $\mathcal N$. Pullback respects tensor products and duals. Apply this equality to the four sheaves $\mathcal O_X$, $\mathcal O_X(D)^\vee$, $\mathcal O_X(D')^\vee$, and their tensor product in the defining Euler-characteristic expression for intersection. The result is $\pi^*D\cdot\pi^*D'=D\cdot D'$, including the self-intersection case. [F5, F6, F7, step 3.1]

5.1 For the reduced curve through $p$, the proved point formula gives $\pi^*C=C'+mE$. Orthogonality and symmetry imply $0=E\cdot C'+mE^2$, hence $C'\cdot E=mr$. Bilinearity and step 4.2 give $C^2=(C'+mE)^2=(C')^2+2m^2r-m^2r$, so $(C')^2=C^2-m^2r$. If $p\notin C$, a local equation is a unit near $p$; its pullback misses $E$, and the off-center isomorphism gives $\pi^*C=C'$. The same pullback identity yields $(C')^2=C^2$. Choice enters only through the recorded suppliers. [F1, F6, F7, F8, step 4.1, step 4.2] ∎

title: Intersection Products on Smooth Projective Surfaces — Examples

items.title: The intersection pairing on the projective plane
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited through the Euler-characteristic and cohomology suppliers. Let k be a field and X = P^2_k with twisting sheaves O(d). Then O(d) . O(e) = de for all d,e in Z. Consequently the class l := O(1) of a line satisfies l . l = 1, and for nonzero homogeneous forms f, g of degrees d,e >= 1 with zero schemes C = Z(f), D = Z(g) and O(C) = O(d), O(D) = O(e) (effective Cartier divisors) one has C . D = de; in particular a line l has l . l = 1, a smooth conic C has C . C = 4, a line and a smooth conic meet with l . C = 2 = deg_l(O(2)|_l). All values lie in Z and agree with the restriction-degree theorem.
items.strategy: By thm-cohomology-projective-space-twisting-sheaves, H^q(P^2_k, O(m)) vanishes except for q = 0 and q = 2, with h^0 = binom(m+2,2) for m >= 0 and h^2 = binom(-m-1,2) for m <= -3, so chi(O(m)) = binom(m+2,2) for every m in Z. The definition gives O(d) . O(e) = 1 - binom(2-d,2) - binom(2-e,2) + binom(2-d-e,2), a polynomial identity in d,e equal to de (check on the finitely many residue classes of d,e modulo which the second difference is constant, or expand). For a nonzero form f of degree d, lem-global-section-effective-divisor applied to the nonzero section f of O(d) (regular because P^2_k is integral) gives the effective Cartier divisor C = Z(f) with O(C) = O(d), so C . D = O(d) . O(e) = de. The line case l . l = 1 and the conic case C . C = 4 are the specializations d = e = 1 and d = e = 2, and l . C = 2 is checked independently against thm-intersection-with-curve-as-degree-of-restriction and the explicit cohomology of O(2) on P^1 (ex-cohomology-o-d-projective-line-all-d): deg_l(O(2)|_l) = chi(O(2)) - chi(O) = 3 - 1 = 2. The Axiom of Choice enters through the Euler-characteristic supplier and the published cohomology of twists on projective space; no further choice is made.

items.title: The intersection form of the blown-up projective plane
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited through the Euler-characteristic and
blowup suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field,
$X=\mathbb P^2_k$, let $p\in X(k)$ be a $k$-rational point, let
$\pi:X'=\operatorname{Bl}_pX\to X$ be the blowup
([[def-blowup-scheme-along-ideal]]), let $E=\pi^{-1}(p)$ be the exceptional
curve ([[def-exceptional-divisor-blowup]]) and let
$l:=\pi^*\mathcal O_X(1)$ in $\operatorname{Pic}(X')$ (the pullback of the
hyperplane class; it is also the strict transform of any line not passing
through $p$). Then
$$l\cdot l=1,\qquad l\cdot E=0,\qquad E\cdot E=-1,$$
so the intersection form on the sublattice $\mathbb Zl+\mathbb ZE$ of
$\operatorname{Pic}(X')$ has matrix
$$\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$
Moreover the strict transform $m:=\pi^*\mathcal O(1)-E$ of a line through $p$
([[def-strict-transform-closed-subscheme]]) satisfies $m=l-E$, $m\cdot E=1$
and $m\cdot m=0$.
items.strategy:
**Given:** a field $k$, the plane $X=\mathbb P^2_k$, a $k$-rational point $p$, the blowup $\pi:X'=\operatorname{Bl}_pX\to X$, its exceptional curve $E$, the class $l=\pi^*\mathcal O_X(1)$, and a line $L$ through $p$.

1.1 The blowup data. Since $p$ is $k$-rational, $r=1$; the surface $X'$ is integral regular projective and $E$ is an effective Cartier divisor isomorphic to $\mathbb P^1_k$ with $\mathcal O_E(E)\cong\mathcal O(-1)$, so the intersection product is defined on $X'$ and $E^2=-r=-1$; moreover $E\cdot\pi^*D=0$ and $\pi^*D\cdot\pi^*D'=D\cdot D'$ for all Cartier divisors $D,D'$ on $X$. [F2]

1.2 $l\cdot l=1$. Choose a line $L'$ on $X$; its class satisfies $[\mathcal O_X(L')]=[\mathcal O_X(1)]$, so $l\cdot l=\pi^*\mathcal O_X(L')\cdot\pi^*\mathcal O_X(L')=\mathcal O_X(L')\cdot\mathcal O_X(L')=1$ by the pullback identity and the plane computation. [F1, F2, F3]

1.3 $l\cdot E=0$. With $D$ the Cartier divisor of any line on $X$, so that $\pi^*D$ has class $l$, the orthogonality clause gives $E\cdot\pi^*D=0$, that is, $l\cdot E=E\cdot l=0$ by symmetry. [F2, F3]

2.1 $E\cdot E=-1$. This is the self-intersection formula of step 1.1 with $r=1$. [F2, step 1.1]

3.1 The matrix. Steps 1.2, 1.3 and 2.1 give $l\cdot l=1$, $l\cdot E=0=E\cdot l$ and $E\cdot E=-1$; if $al+bE=0$ in $\operatorname{Pic}(X\prime)$, pairing with $l$ gives $a=0$ and pairing with $E$ gives $-b=0$. Thus these classes freely generate the stated sublattice; by bilinearity its Gram matrix of the sublattice $\mathbb Zl+\mathbb ZE$ in the basis $(l,E)$ is $\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$. [F1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.1]

3.2 The strict transform of a line through $p$. Let $L$ be a line through $p$ with strict transform $m$. The line is reduced and its multiplicity at $p$ is $1$, so $\pi^*L=m+E$ and $m\cdot E=1$ and $m\cdot m=L\cdot L-1=0$; equivalently, taking classes and using $\mathcal O_{X'}(\pi^*L)\cong\pi^*\mathcal O_X(1)$, the class of $m$ is $l-E$, and bilinearity and steps 1.2–2.1 give $m\cdot E=l\cdot E-E\cdot E=0+1=1$ and $m\cdot m=l\cdot l-2l\cdot E+E\cdot E=1-0-1=0$, in agreement. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.1]

4.1 Conclusion and choice accounting. Steps 1.2, 1.3 and 2.1 give the matrix of the intersection form on $\mathbb Zl+\mathbb ZE$, and step 3.2 gives $m=l-E$, $m\cdot E=1$, $m\cdot m=0$ for the strict transform of a line through $p$. The Axiom of Choice enters through the suppliers recorded in [F4]; the point, the lines and the blowup are given data and no selection is made in the computations. [F4, step 3.1, step 3.2] ∎

items.title: The intersection product needs Cartier or complementary-dimension hypotheses
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited through the Euler-characteristic supplier. The claim refuted: (a) every effective prime divisor on a normal integral projective surface over a field is Cartier, so that its self-intersection is defined by the alternating-sum formula of def-divisor-intersection-number-on-smooth-projective-surface; and (b) for every smooth projective k-scheme X of dimension at least two and all effective Cartier divisors D, E on X, the scheme-theoretic intersection D cap E is finite and its length over k equals the alternating sum chi(X,O_X) - chi(X,O_X(-D)) - chi(X,O_X(-E)) + chi(X,O_X(-D-E)).
items.strategy: (a) Let k be a field of characteristic different from 2 and let X = V_+(xy - z^2) in P^3_k be the projective quadric cone with vertex v = [0:0:0:1]. Its affine chart w = 1 is the affine cone Spec k[x,y,z]/(xy - z^2), which is normal and integral, and the published counterexample cex-weil-divisor-not-cartier-singular-cone proves that the prime divisor Z = V(x,z) (the ruling through the vertex) is not Cartier at the vertex: no neighbourhood of the vertex carries a Cartier divisor with associated Weil divisor [Z]. Normality and integrality are local, so X is a normal integral projective surface on which the effective prime divisor Z is not Cartier, and O_X(-Z) does not exist as an invertible sheaf; the definition therefore gives no value Z . Z. (b) Let k be algebraically closed, X = P^3_k, D = V(x_0) (a plane) and E = V(x_1) (another plane). The two divisors are effective Cartier, but D cap E = V(x_0,x_1) is a line, so no finite point count exists; the alternating sum with L = M = O(1) is chi(O) - 2 chi(O(-1)) + chi(O(-2)) = 1 - 0 + 0 = 1, a value unchanged if E is replaced by D, whose intersection with D is 2-dimensional. Hence the sum is not a count of points: the dimension hypothesis dim Supp F <= n in the definition cannot be dropped, and cycles must have complementary dimension for a length interpretation. The Axiom of Choice enters only through the Euler-characteristic supplier and the published counterexample; the two computations make no selection.
